title: It read the menu before we left

slides.headline: It found the restaurant, then //[[gold]]read me the actual menu[[/gold]]
slides.sub: Not a review score. The dishes.

slides.headline: "Is there an Italian place near here, and what's good?"
slides.body: One sentence. Not a search, not a filter, not three apps.

slides.headline: It found real places, with real distances
slides.body: Actual businesses from the map, sorted by how far away they genuinely are — not sponsored listings, not a chain branch four suburbs over.

slides.headline: Then it [[gold]]opened the restaurant's own site[[/gold]]
slides.body: Found the menu link, followed it, and read what's on it. This is the part other assistants skip — they hand you the link and stop.

turns.text: Onesto, about half a mile. Their menu's got a pork belly with honeycomb agrodolce at eighteen, and the pastas are all house-made.
Anything on there I can't eat?
The burrata starter, and I'd ask about the pesto.

slides.headline: "What's good there" is a real question
slides.body: Star ratings tell you a place exists. The menu tells you whether to go. Argus reads the second one.
